report.summary: Reviewed harness.py chunk 2 (lines 281-~520): tier1 loop, arms A/B/C eval, BM25, whole-repo text. Claims mostly kept; one docstring claim about _whole_repo_text cap semantics is broken; one uncheckable.
risks: line ~470 | medium | _whole_repo_text docstring claims cap_chars=None walks ENTIRE repo untruncated, but code leaves dirnames unsorted and skips dot-dirs (same as _repo_chunks), so the 'TRUE size' may exclude dot-directories; also comment 'what Tier 2 actually hands a model' is contradicted by the cap being _DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS*4 not _DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS. | Check whether any repo has non-hidden dot-directories; confirm run_tier2's default cap.
todos: Verify run_tier2's actual default cap to settle the _DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS*4 discrepancy.
Check whether dot-directories under a repo should be excluded from the 'TRUE size' baseline.

handoff.purpose: Tier-1 task loop with error/focus-withheld handling, whole-repo text, BM25 retrieval, and deterministic A/B/C arm evaluation.

symbols.name: _whole_repo_text
symbols.note: Walks root recursively, skips _IGNORE_DIRS and dot-dirs, reads files with errors='replace', concatenates with headers. cap_chars truncates mid-block and returns truncated=True.

symbols.name: _target_query
symbols.note: Extracts query from target: after '::' if present, else file stem.

symbols.name: _repo_chunks
symbols.note: Walks root with sorted dirnames, extracts units via extract_units, falls back to whole file; returns list of (label, source).

symbols.name: _BM25_TOKEN_RE
symbols.note: Regex for BM25 tokens: identifiers starting with letter/underscore.

symbols.name: _bm25_scores
symbols.note: Compute Okapi BM25 scores with k1=1.2, b=0.75; ties broken by caller.

symbols.name: _bm25_context
symbols.note: Top-k BM25 retrieval up to budget_tokens; always includes best chunk even if over budget; returns text, counts, truncated flag.

symbols.name: _DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS
symbols.note: Constant 120_000, used as cap for B in eval_task_arms.

symbols.name: eval_task_arms
symbols.note: Deterministic A/B/C comparison: semantic slice vs whole-repo vs BM25. Returns dict with recall and token counts. Guards correctness tasks, resolution errors, focus-withheld.

claims.text: A single unresolvable task ... is caught here too, not just inside eval_task_tier1: this loop resolves the repo/builds the index ITSELF ... so that resolution step needs its own guard.
claims.why: The loop calls resolve_task_repo and cached_index inside a try/except (ValueError, OSError) and appends _task_error_row on failure.

claims.text: ERRORED rows land in both per_task (never silently dropped -- "a degraded measurement is reported, never silent") and the dedicated errored list, and are excluded from by_provenance
claims.why: per_task receives _task_error_row; errored is filtered from per_task; healthy excludes rows with 'error' in t; _by_provenance is called with healthy.

claims.text: n_tasks/n_primary_tasks/n_quarantine_tasks remain simple total-attempted counts over label alone (unaffected by error status, and therefore byte-identical to before this existed for any store with zero errored tasks); n_errored_tasks is new and additive.
claims.why: n = len(per_task) includes errored rows; n_primary counts by label_tier only; n_quarantine = n - n_primary; n_errored_tasks = len(errored) is separate.

claims.text: Refused BEFORE the repo is resolved, not only inside eval_task_tier1: this loop does its own resolution for the index cache, and a correctness task is not required to carry anything this harness can resolve.
claims.why: is_correctness_task(task) is checked before resolve_task_repo and appends _correctness_task_row.

claims.text: FOCUS-WITHHELD ... Excluded from `healthy` (therefore from every mean/miss count in by_provenance) same as errored rows, and separately counted/named so it is reported, never silently folded into either a pass or a miss.
claims.why: focus_withheld is filtered by t.get('focus_withheld'); healthy excludes focus_withheld; n_focus_withheld and focus_withheld_ids are in the return dict.

claims.text: cap_chars=None (the new default) walks the ENTIRE repo untruncated -- the TRUE size of the baseline.
claims.why: The code skips directories in _IGNORE_DIRS and any directory starting with '.', so it does not walk the ENTIRE repo; dot-directories are excluded. The claim 'TRUE size' is overstated.

claims.text: Pass an int to cap it (what Tier 2 actually hands a model). Returns (text, truncated); truncated is always False when uncapped.
claims.why: When cap_chars is an int, the cap is applied and truncated may be True; but the claim 'what Tier 2 actually hands a model' is contradicted by eval_task_arms using cap_chars=_DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS*4, not _DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS. 'truncated is always False when uncapped' is kept because uncapped path never sets truncated=True.

claims.text: Retrieval units for arm C: one chunk per extractable unit (function or class), else the whole file when nothing is extractable -- "the repo's files/units" the BM25 baseline retrieves over. Same source-file universe as _whole_repo_text.
claims.why: extract_units is used per file; if units exist each becomes a chunk, else the whole file text is used. Both functions use os.walk with the same _IGNORE_DIRS and dot-dir filter, so the universe matches.

claims.text: Unlike _whole_repo_text, dirnames ARE sorted here: this is new code with no prior byte-order contract to preserve, and BM25 tie-breaking needs a deterministic candidate order.
claims.why: dirnames[:] = sorted(...) in _repo_chunks; _whole_repo_text does not sort dirnames.

claims.text: Okapi BM25 over pre-tokenized docs -- no new dependency, no network. Standard k1=1.2 / b=0.75.
claims.why: The implementation uses math.log and standard BM25 formula with k1=1.2, b=0.75; no network or external deps.

claims.text: Ties are broken by the CALLER (chunk label, not insertion order) so retrieval order stays deterministic regardless of dict/set iteration order (PYTHONHASHSEED).
claims.why: _bm25_scores returns scores only; _bm25_context sorts by (-scores[i], chunks[i][0]) using the label as tiebreaker.

claims.text: Top-k BM25 retrieval up to budget_tokens -- arm C. Chunks are taken whole, never split mid-chunk; the single best-ranked chunk is always included even if it alone exceeds budget (an empty context is a strictly worse baseline than a slightly-over one).
claims.why: The loop picks blocks whole; the first chunk is added unconditionally because 'if picked and total + t > budget_tokens' only breaks when picked is non-empty.

claims.text: truncated is True iff a lower-ranked chunk existed that did not fit the remaining budget.
claims.why: truncated is set only when a chunk does not fit and picked is non-empty; if no such chunk exists it remains False.

claims.text: A = the distilled semantic slice (today's product). B = naive whole-repo concat. Recall is measured against the TRUE, FULL, UNTRUNCATED text (tokens_B) -- beating a baseline you truncated is not a win.
claims.why: text_b_full is generated with cap_chars=None (though dot-dirs excluded, the claim about truncation holds for the walk); recall_b is computed on text_b_full.

claims.text: tokens_B_capped_at_default/b_truncated_at_cap additionally report what Tier 2 would actually hand a model (capped at _DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS), so that weakening is visible, not hidden inside a smaller B that looks stronger than it is.
claims.why: The code uses cap_chars=_DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS*4, not _DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS. The comment above _DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS also says it mirrors run_tier2's default, but the multiplication by 4 contradicts the claim that the cap is _DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS.

claims.text: C = BM25 top-k retrieval, budgeted to the SAME token count as A (token_budget_C == tokens_A) -- the 'dumb retrieval' baseline that matters commercially.
claims.why: budget_c = max(tokens_a, 1) and _bm25_context is called with budget_tokens=budget_c.

claims.text: c_beats_a is TIE-INCLUSIVE (recall_C >= recall_A, matching the report's 'C>=A' column and this module's own docstring promise that a tie is 'reported loudly, not smoothed over')
claims.why: The return dict is cut off before the c_beats_a key is shown; the comparison itself is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: NEVER RAISES: same per-task resolution guard as eval_task_tier1 -- a ValueError/OSError resolving the repo or slicing the target returns an ERRORED row (_task_error_row) instead of propagating.
claims.why: The try block wraps resolve_task_repo, cached_index, _repo_chunks, and semantic_slice, catching (ValueError, OSError) and returning _task_error_row.

claims.text: A CORRECTNESS task is likewise refused (_correctness_task_row) rather than scored: all three arms here go through _recall, so a task with no must_include would read as a perfect 1.0 in every arm at once.
claims.why: is_correctness_task(task) is checked first and returns _correctness_task_row(task).

observations.what: _whole_repo_text docstring claims 'walks the ENTIRE repo' but the implementation skips dot-directories and _IGNORE_DIRS, so the 'TRUE size' baseline may exclude hidden directories.

eval_task_arms uses cap_chars=_DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS*4 for the capped B, while the docstring says 'capped at _DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS' and the comment above the constant says it mirrors run_tier2's default. This is a 4x discrepancy.

The tier1 loop's per_task list includes _correctness_task_row and _task_error_row, which may not have a 'label_tier' key; _is_primary_tier is called on every row. If _is_primary_tier assumes the key exists, it could raise. The docstring says n_primary is over label alone, but error/correctness rows may lack that label.

In _whole_repo_text, when cap_chars is reached mid-file, the block is truncated and returned immediately, but the code does not include the remainder of the file. The docstring says 'cap it (what Tier 2 actually hands a model)' -- if the cap is meant to be a token budget, the character-based cap may not align with token counts.
